build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel and its four pinned dependency wheels by hash (pip --require-hashes, then pip check); the image checks that the wheel mo_sql_parsing/ package is byte-identical to the pinned sdist and that mo_sql_parsing/sql_parser.py and the MPL-2.0 LICENSE match recorded SHA-256 values.
dependencies_note: mo-parsing 9.3.26234 (MIT) is the parsing engine that runs the mo-sql-parsing grammar; mo-dots 10.688.26234, mo-future 7.687.26234 and mo-imports 7.687.26234 are its pinned helper libraries from the same author. The fuzz entry point is an external one-file Python bridge (linux/arm64 has no Atheris 3.1.0 cp314 wheel); the parser-line AFL++ bridge runs natively on arm64 to stay within afl-showmap's 30 s per-run limit.
parser_family: mo-sql-parsing SQL grammar (mo_sql_parsing/sql_parser.py, keywords.py, types.py) on the mo-parsing combinator engine (a pyparsing-derived library by the same author); independent of sqlparse, sqlglot, sqlfluff, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs
dialect: mo-sql-parsing common parser (mo_sql_parsing.parse, the generic entry point; parse_mysql, parse_sqlserver and parse_bigquery are not used)
api: mo_sql_parsing.parse(local SQL text decoded from UTF-8 bytes) -> JSON parse tree (select/from/where/groupby/orderby or insert/values mappings); the harness walks those keys, {operator_or_function: arguments} expressions (operators identified by mo_sql_parsing.keywords.precedence), {"literal": text} strings and numeric values
fuzz_engine: external one-file Python bridge for AFL++ and generator replay
coverage: Python line tracing of the mo_sql_parsing and mo_parsing package sources during valid-control replay; the AFL++ bridge maps the same traced lines
scope: One SQL statement from local text via mo_sql_parsing.parse; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. The dialect-specific entry points, the formatter and NULL/call customisation options are untested.
